 (Resp.No.2 - By Sri.Ravi S Samprathi, Adv.)
 J U D G M E N T

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .80,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Sri.Jagadish.V S/o.Late Venkateshappa in a road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 23.01.2024 at about 04.00 p.m., when deceased Jagadish.V. was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-50-X-1176, on Tumkuru - Bengaluru NH-48 Service road, near Madavara Metro Station, Bengaluru, a Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AB-9978 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against deceased's motor cycle resulting in accident.

Due to said accident, deceased sustained multiple injuries and thereafter shifted to Abhay Vashistha Hospital, Madanayakanahalli,
Bengaluru, wherein he succumbed to the injuries at the hospital.

Later body was shifted to General Hospital, Nelamangala, wherein postmortem was conducted and body was handed over to petitioners to perform funeral and obsequies ceremonies for which they have spent a sum of .2,00,000/- and .1,00,000/- towards medical expenses and transportation of body.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was doing business and construction work and earning a sum of .40,000/- per month.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners lost bread earning member of the family and put to lot of mental agony.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of canter by its driver.

The respondent No.1 & 2, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed written statement.

Divya P vs Keshava Murthy on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199725151/
2
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of deceased as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further contended that the driver of canter was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
Further the driver of canter was not holding valid permit and route permit and FC as on the date of accident.
Further this respondent has issued policy of insurance in favour of first respondent pertaining to lorry and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that on the date of accident, the canter was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of driver of canter.
Further the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of deceased.

The deceased,
being rider of motor cycle, without having proper look out for vehicular movements on the road and was riding motor cycle recklessly and carelessly and while trying to overtake canter from its left side,
collided with canter that resulted in accident.
The IMV Report demonstrates that the deceased dashed against the hind portion of the canter while riding motor cycle and caused the accident.
As such the accident took place due to negligence on the part of deceased himself and not due to the negligence on the part of driver of canter.
Further contended that at the time of accident, the deceased was not wearing ISI Mark headgear and was not holding valid and effective driving license.
The amount claimed by petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Jagadish.V succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 23.01.2024 at about 04.00 p.m., when deceased was riding motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-50-X-1176, on Tumkuru-Bengaluru NH-48 Service Road, Near Madavara Metro Station, Bengaluru,
due to the rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AB-9978 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to substantiate the contention of the petition, the Petitioner No.1/wife of deceased got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15 and closed evidence of petitioners' side.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. Heard arguments on both side and perused the materials available on records.
8.
This Tribunal answers the above issues as below:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Divya P vs Keshava Murthy on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199725151/
3  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.

It is the case of the petitioners that deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 23.01.2024 at about 04.00 p.m., when deceased was riding motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-50-X-1176, on Tumkuru-Bengaluru NH-48 Service Road, Near Madavara Metro Station, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-05- AB-9978 by its driver.
10. The Petitioner No.1/wife of deceased Sri.Jagadish.V got examined as PW.1.

In the chief- examination, PW.1 deposed that accident occurred while her husband was riding his motor cycle,
due to the rash and negligent driving of canter by its driver.

In order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of canter, the petitioners produced Ex.P.2 First Information statement lodged by one of the relatives by name Sri.Puneeth Kumar.L with police on 23.01.2024.
On the basis of first information lodged, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 304(A) of IPC.
In first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of canter by its driver.
The petitioners also furnished spot mahazar & sketch which are marked as Ex.P.3 & 4.
The said documents disclose that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said documents.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that the actual facts at the place of accident are contrary to the facts as shown in the mahazar and sketch.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report, wherein damages caused to both the vehicles are mentioned.
The IMV report discloses the aspect of offending vehicle being damaged.
If the offending vehicle is not involved in the accident, then the vehicle could not have been damaged.
The owner or driver of offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages are caused to the vehicle.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Ex . P.6
is the Inquest Report
. Ex.P7 is the PM report, wherein deceased Sri.Jagadish.V is stated to have died due to shock and haemorrhage as a result of multiple injuries sustained.
Ex . P8 is the notice issued under Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given to said notice is marked as Ex.P9.
In Ex.P8, notice given by I.O, it is mentioned that the lorry is involved in the accident and that the negligence of driver of the lorry is the cause for the accident.
The respondent No.1, owner of the lorry, appears to have given reply to the said notice as per Ex P-9.

In the reply given to the notice,
respondent No.1 could have denied the involvement of lorry or negligence on the part of driver of lorry, in the cause of accident.
There is no recital in the reply to the notice denying involvement of vehicle and negligence of driver.
Further, respondent No.1 could have explained the manner in which the lorry got damaged, as mentioned in IMV report.
But, there is no explanation in the reply regarding the manner in which canter being damaged.

The I.O., after detailed investigation, filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 304(A)
of IPC as per Ex.P.10.

In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash Divya P vs Keshava Murthy on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199725151/
4 and negligent driving of canter by its driver.
In the final report, there is no mention about negligence on the part of rider of the motor cycle.
The documents furnished by petitioners disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of canter in the cause of accident.
The respondents not placed any materials in order to rebut or disprove the documents furnished by the petitioners related to the aspect of negligence.
The owner or driver of the canter does not appear to have challenged the FIR as well as final report filed by the police against the driver of offending vehicle.
The correctness of investigation does not appear to have been challenged by respondents in any manner.
In the cross examination of PW.1 also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited from the witness.

Nothing to doubt the involvement of offending vehicle or dispute the aspect of negligence of driver of offending vehicle, could be elicited in the cross examination of PW.1.
11.
The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by the petitioners are to be looked into in order to ascertain the aspect of negligence.
The materials placed before the Tribunal points towards the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
So, the oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioners discloses that the accident was caused due to rash and negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of petitioners coupled with the documents produced before this tribunal, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AB-9978 by its driver and deceased succumbed to injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc.
(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings: (i) In the petition the age of the deceased Sri.Jagadish.V is shown as 42 years.

In order to prove age of deceased, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.14 & 15 - Notarized copy of driving license and Adhaar Card,
wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 09.06.1981.
As per the documents furnished by petitioners, the age of the deceased appears to be 42 years at the time of accident.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to dispute or rebut the document furnished by petitioners related to the age of deceased.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the document furnished by petitioners is to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
The accident occurred on 23.01.2023.
As per the materials furnished before the Tribunal, the age of deceased was 42 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Smt. Sarla Verma case multiplier applicable in the present case is '14'.
( ii) The petitioners contended that deceased Sri.Jagadish.V was doing business and building construction work and earning a sum of .40,000/- per month.
In order to prove the occupation and income of deceased, the petitioners not furnished satisfactory materials.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to substantiate the contention of petitioners related to occupation and income of deceased.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials related to occupation and income of deceased, notional income is to be considered.

By considering Divya P vs Keshava Murthy on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199725151/
5 the facts and circumstances of case, the notional income of deceased is considered as .16,000/- per month.

In Hem Raj V/s the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there cannot be distinction where there is positive evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guess work in the facts and circumstances of a case.

entities.text: Hem Raj V/s the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Both the situations stand at the same footing.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, the petitioners are entitled for future prospects.

In National Insurance Company Ltd V/s Pranaya Sethi and others case the Hon'be Supreme Court held that, in case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 25% of the established income should be warranted where the deceased was aged between 40 to 50 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd V/s Pranaya Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand deceased was aged about 42 years.
Hence, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners are entitled for additional 25% to the established income.

The established income of the deceased is .16,000/- and 25% of .16,000/-
is .4,000/-.
So, the total gross income of deceased was .16,000/- + .4,000/- = .20,000/- per month.
As per the materials on record, the deceased Sri.Jagadish.V is married, having wife, children and mother.
In order to prove the same, the petitioners have produced notarized copies of Aadhaar cards which are marked as Ex.P13 to 15.
On perusal of the same it reveals that petitioners No.1 to 4 are wife, children and mother respectively.
The said documents disclose the relationship of petitioners with that of the deceased.
The materials on record disclose that petitioners are dependents on the income of deceased.
Hence, petitioner No.1 to 4 are considered as dependents of deceased.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Smt.Sarla Verma case, where number of dependent family members is 4 to 6, 1/4th is to be deducted from the gross income of deceased towards his personal expenses and remaining is to be taken as income towards dependency.

Thus,
petitioners are entitled to compensation of .25,20,000/- towards loss of dependency which is calculated as follows:
Calculation Total (In .)
1/4th of .20,000/- (deduction . 15,000/-
 of .5,000/-)
.15,000/- multiply by 12 .1,80,000/-
.1,80,000/- multiply by 14 .25,20,000/-
 Multiplier
(B) Towards Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses;
In the case on hand, the date of accident was on 23.01.2023.

In view of ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Pranay Sethi case, the petitioners are entitled for additional 10% on conventional heads which is to be enhanced on percentage basis in every three years and the enhancement should be at the rate of 10% in a span of three years.

So the petitioner No.1 to 4 being the wife, children and mother of deceased are entitled for .48,400/- (each) towards loss of Spousal Consortium, Parental Consortium and Filial Consortium and also entitled for .18,150/- towards loss of estate and .18,150/- towards funeral expenses.

6 (C) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioners claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that her husband took treatment at the Hospital.
The petitioner produced medical bills amounting to .53,358/- which are marked as Ex.P.12.
The said documents disclose the aspect of treatment availed by husband of petitioner No.1 and the expenses incurred for the treatment.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to controvert or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner related to the medical expenses.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by petitioner is to be considered.
So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .53,358/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.

13. Thus, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation as follows:

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of .28,03,258/-.

14. In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: 15. The petitioners filed petition against the respondent No.1 & 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AB-9978 by its driver.
There appears to be no dispute with respect to the ownership of respondent No.1 pertaining to offending vehicle and issue of policy of insurance by respondent No.2 pertaining to offending vehicle.

The materials on record disclose that the offending vehicle was having valid and effective policy of insurance and the driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective licence at the time of accident.
So, the respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.

7 16.
Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of .28,03,258/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakhs Three Thousand Two Hundred and Fifty Eight only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitione.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioner No.1 being the wife of deceased is entitled for 40%, petitioner No.2 & 3 being the minor children of deceased are entitled for 20% each and petitioner No.4 being the mother of deceased is entitled for 20% of the compensation amount.
In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.1 & 4, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 & 4, and 40% of the amount shall be kept in FD.

20% each of compensation amount allotted shall be kept in FD in the names of minor petitioner No.2 & 3 in any of the Nationalized Bank or Scheduled Bank of the choice of minor guardian for a period of 3 years or till they attains the age of majority whichever is later.
The guardian of petitioner is entitled to receive interest that accrues on FD periodically.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioners hereby directed to produce particulars of Bank Account of petitioners,
with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioners, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioners shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioners are entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.

Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioners on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to their account after expiry of three years period of deposit, without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Office to draw Award accordingly.
